steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: import
React
useState
'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState from 'react'. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react' in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using a single import statement.

steps.title: Create the main component function
steps.instruction: Create a function component named OptimisticUI that returns JSX.Element. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.hint: Define a component function that returns a JSX element (like a div). Make sure to include the return type : JSX.Element for TypeScript.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the OptimisticUI component function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named OptimisticUI is defined with a return statement that outputs JSX.
successCriteria: The component is named OptimisticUI, returns JSX (e.g., a div), and has the correct return type annotation : JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the OptimisticUI component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named OptimisticUI, returns JSX (like a div), and includes the return type : JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it OptimisticUI, used a return statement with JSX, and added the TypeScript return type.

steps.title: Define the data interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface called TodoItem with three properties: id (number), text (string), and completed (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TodoItem interface is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The interface must be named TodoItem and include id: number, text: string, and completed: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TodoItem interface with the correct property types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface is named TodoItem and includes all three properties with the correct types: id (number), text (string), and completed (boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Please define a TodoItem interface with id: number, text: string, and completed: boolean properties.

steps.title: Initialize the todos state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'todos' initialized with an empty array. The array should contain TodoItem objects (use the interface you defined earlier).
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial value that matches the TodoItem[] type. The hook returns an array where the first element is the state variable and the second is the setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a todos state variable initialized with an empty array (or sample data) that follows the TodoItem interface structure.
successCriteria: useState hook is called
State variable is named 'todos'
Initial value is an array
Array contains TodoItem objects (or is empty)
Type annotation TodoItem[] is used
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the todos state with the correct type. The state is now ready to store your todo items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you're using the useState hook correctly and that the initial value is an array of TodoItem objects (or an empty array). Also ensure you're using the TodoItem[] type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to call useState to create a state variable named 'todos'. The initial value should be an array (empty or with sample TodoItem objects), and you should use the TodoItem[] type annotation.

steps.title: Initialize loading state
steps.instruction: Inside your OptimisticUI component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'loading' initialized to false. This will track when operations are in progress.
steps.hint: Add a second useState call after your todos state. Remember to use TypeScript generics to specify the type as boolean.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a loading state
const [loading, setLoading] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will now have a loading state variable that can be used to track when operations are in progress.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call that creates a 'loading' variable initialized to false with boolean type annotation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a loading state variable. This will help track when operations are in progress for optimistic updates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're creating a state variable called 'loading' with the boolean type and initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating just the loading state. Use useState<boolean>(false) to create a variable named 'loading'.

steps.title: Define the addTodo function
steps.instruction: Inside your OptimisticUI component, define an async function named addTodo that takes a string parameter (the todo text) and returns void.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to mark it as async since it will eventually handle API calls.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an empty async addTodo function that will later implement optimistic updates.
successCriteria: Function named addTodo exists
Function is marked as async
Function takes a string parameter
Function returns void or Promise<void>
Function is defined inside the component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the addTodo function. This will be the foundation for implementing optimistic updates in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: 1) Is the function named exactly 'addTodo'? 2) Is it marked as async? 3) Does it take a string parameter? 4) Is it defined inside the component?
steps.feedbackWrong: The addTodo function wasn't properly defined. Make sure to create an async function named addTodo that takes a string parameter and returns void, defined inside the OptimisticUI component.

steps.title: Define the toggleTodo function
steps.instruction: Inside the OptimisticUI component, define an async function named toggleTodo that takes a todo id parameter and toggles its completed status with optimistic UI updates.
steps.hint: Create an async function that accepts an id parameter. Inside, first update the todos state optimistically, then simulate an API call with setTimeout, and handle potential rollback on error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleTodo function is defined with proper TypeScript typing, optimistic updates, and error handling.
successCriteria: Function named toggleTodo is defined
Function is async
Accepts id parameter with type number
Updates todos state optimistically before API simulation
Includes try-catch for error handling with rollback
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggleTodo function with optimistic updates. The function first updates the UI immediately, then simulates an API call, and handles potential errors by rolling back the changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Is the function async? Does it accept an id parameter? Does it update the todos state optimistically before the simulated API call? Does it include error handling with rollback?
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTodo function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create an async function that takes a todo id, updates the todos state optimistically, simulates an API call, and handles errors by rolling back changes.

steps.title: Return the main container
steps.instruction: Return a JSX fragment containing a div with a heading that says 'Optimistic UI Demo'.
steps.hint: The return statement should output a div with an h1 element inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a heading 'Optimistic UI Demo' inside a div container.
successCriteria: The return statement should include a div element containing an h1 element with the text 'Optimistic UI Demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the main container with the heading. This provides the basic structure for your Optimistic UI demo.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div with an h1 element containing exactly 'Optimistic UI Demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't match the expected structure. Please ensure you're returning a div with an h1 element inside it.

steps.title: Add the todo list display
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, add a <ul> element that maps through the todos state array and displays each todo item as a <li> element. Each list item should show the todo text.
steps.hint: Use the todos state array with the map method. Inside the map callback, return a <li> element with the todo text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of todos below the heading.
successCriteria: A <ul> element is added inside the return statement
The todos array is mapped using the map method
Each todo item is rendered as a <li> element
Each <li> displays the todo text content
Each <li> has a unique key prop using todo.id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the todo list from state. Each todo item is now displayed as a list item with its text content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all required elements: a <ul> element, mapping through todos, rendering <li> elements with todo text, and providing unique key props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todo list isn't displaying correctly. Make sure you add a <ul> element that maps through the todos state array and renders each item as a <li> with the todo text.

steps.title: Add todo items with toggle buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, map over the todos array to render each todo item as a list item (<li>) containing a checkbox and the todo text. The checkbox should be wired to call the toggleTodo function when clicked, passing the todo's id.
steps.hint: Use the todos.map() method to iterate. Each list item needs a checkbox input with type='checkbox', checked={todo.completed}, and onChange={() => toggleTodo(todo.id)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of todo items, each with a checkbox that can be toggled (though the toggleTodo function is not yet implemented).
successCriteria: The code must include a map over todos to create <li> elements, each containing a checkbox input with checked={todo.completed} and onChange={() => toggleTodo(todo.id)}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added interactive todo items with checkboxes. The UI now displays each todo with a toggle button, ready to be wired to the toggle functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each todo item has a checkbox input with the correct checked and onChange attributes. Check that you're mapping over todos and using todo.completed and todo.id correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todo items aren't displaying correctly. Ensure you're using todos.map() to create list items, each with a checkbox that has checked={todo.completed} and onChange={() => toggleTodo(todo.id)}.

steps.title: Add the add todo form
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add a form with an input field and a submit button to allow users to add new todos. The form should call the addTodo function when submitted.
steps.hint: Create a form element with an onSubmit handler. Inside the form, add an input for the todo text and a submit button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now includes a form with an input and a submit button. When the form is submitted, it should call the addTodo function with the input value.
successCriteria: The code includes a form element with an onSubmit handler that calls addTodo. Inside the form, there is an input field and a submit button.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the form to create new todos. The form is properly wired to call the addTodo function when submitted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some form elements, but make sure you have a complete form with an onSubmit handler that calls addTodo, an input field, and a submit button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form is missing or incomplete. Ensure you add a form element with an onSubmit handler that calls addTodo, an input field, and a submit button inside the main container.

steps.title: Add loading indicator
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering inside your component's return statement to show a loading message when the loading state is true.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or logical && to conditionally render a loading element based on the loading state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display a loading indicator when the loading state is true, providing visual feedback during async operations.
successCriteria: The code includes conditional rendering that checks the loading state variable and displays a loading message or element when it's true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the loading state. This provides visual feedback to users when operations are in progress.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the loading indicator might not be working correctly. Make sure you're using the loading state variable in your conditional rendering and that it displays something when loading is true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading indicator isn't implemented correctly. You need to add conditional rendering that checks the loading state variable and displays a loading message or element when it's true.
